# Task states

Every state the visualizer can show, as described in `celery_viz/states.json`. The UI renders this same data, so this page and the screen cannot disagree.

**Reported** states are what Celery itself says. **Derived** states (marked `≈` in the UI) are this monitor's inference from missing or contradictory events; Celery does not report them.

## Stages

The columns a task's ball moves through, left to right.

| Stage | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Broker queue | The message is stored by the broker, waiting for a consumer. |
| Reserved by a worker | A worker has taken the message but is not running it yet. |
| Running | A pool process is executing the task. |
| Outcome | How this attempt ended. |
| Lost | No worker is known to be holding this task any more. |

## Overview

| State | Kind | Celery state | Celery event | Stage | Needs attention? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Queued](#queued) | reported | PENDING | task-sent | Broker queue | no |
| [Reserved](#received) | reported | RECEIVED | task-received | Reserved by a worker | no |
| [Waiting for ETA](#waiting_eta) | derived ≈ | RECEIVED | task-received (with eta) | Reserved by a worker | no |
| [Running](#started) | reported | STARTED | task-started | Running | no |
| [Succeeded](#success) | reported | SUCCESS | task-succeeded | Outcome | no |
| [Failed](#failure) | reported | FAILURE | task-failed | Outcome | no |
| [Retrying](#retry) | reported | RETRY | task-retried | Outcome | no |
| [Rejected](#rejected) | reported | REJECTED | task-rejected | Outcome | no |
| [Revoked](#revoked) | reported | REVOKED | task-revoked | Outcome | no |
| [Replaced](#replaced) | derived ≈ | — | (none: inferred) | Outcome | no |
| [Ended silently](#ended_silently) | derived ≈ | — | (none: inferred from worker-heartbeat 'active') | Outcome | no |
| [Worker lost](#worker_lost) | derived ≈ | — | (none: absence of worker-heartbeat) | Lost | **yes** |
| [Draining](#draining) | derived ≈ | STARTED | worker-offline (while the task is still running) | Running | no |
| [Suspected hung](#suspected_hung) | derived ≈ | STARTED | task-started (and nothing since) | Running | **yes** |
| [Unknown state](#unknown) | fallback | — | — | Outcome | **yes** |

## Details

### QUEUED

**Queued** (reported by Celery)

Published to the broker; waiting for a worker with a free slot.

Celery reports this as PENDING, but PENDING also means "I have never heard of this task id", so 'queued' here is inferred from the task-sent event, which only exists if the publisher sets task_send_sent_event. With worker_prefetch_multiplier=1 a message waits here until a worker slot is free; with a higher multiplier it may instead sit 'reserved' inside a busy worker while others idle.

Settings that change this:

- [`task_send_sent_event`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/configuration.html#std-setting-task_send_sent_event): Without it the publisher emits no task-sent event and this state is never seen.
- [`worker_prefetch_multiplier`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/configuration.html#std-setting-worker_prefetch_multiplier): Decides how many messages a worker reserves in advance.

### RECEIVED

**Reserved** (reported by Celery)

A worker has taken the message but has not started executing it.

The broker still counts the message as unacknowledged. With acks_late=False it is acknowledged just before execution begins; with acks_late=True only after the task finishes.

Settings that change this:

- [`task_acks_late`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/tasks.html#Task.acks_late): When the message is acknowledged: before running (default) or after it finishes.
- [`worker_prefetch_multiplier`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/configuration.html#std-setting-worker_prefetch_multiplier): Messages sit in this state when a worker reserves more than it can run.

### WAITING_ETA

**Waiting for ETA** (derived by this monitor)

Received, but not allowed to run until its ETA/countdown.

Derived by this monitor: Celery has no SCHEDULED state. This is how retry(countdown=...) and exponential backoff wait: the worker holds the task in memory until the time arrives. On quorum queues, Celery's native delayed delivery holds it in the broker instead.

Settings that change this:

- [`retry_backoff`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/tasks.html#Task.retry_backoff): Produces the growing delays you see here.

### STARTED

**Running** (reported by Celery)

A pool process is executing the task right now.

The task-started event is sent when execution begins. The result-backend STARTED state additionally needs task_track_started. If the worker dies while a task is here: with acks_late=False the message was already acknowledged, so the task is lost; with acks_late=True the broker requeues it.

Settings that change this:

- [`task_track_started`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/tasks.html#Task.track_started): Makes the result backend report STARTED instead of PENDING.
- [`task_acks_late`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/tasks.html#Task.acks_late): Decides whether a worker death here loses the task.

### SUCCESS

**Succeeded** (reported by Celery)

The task returned normally.

The result is stored in the result backend (if one is configured) and, with acks_late=True, the message is acknowledged now.


### FAILURE

**Failed** (reported by Celery)

The task raised an exception that was not retried.

Celery stores the exception. By default the message is still acknowledged on failure (task_acks_on_failure_or_timeout=True), so a failed task is not redelivered. In a chord, a failed header task means the callback never runs.

Settings that change this:

- [`task_acks_on_failure_or_timeout`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/configuration.html#std-setting-task_acks_on_failure_or_timeout): True by default: failures are not redelivered.

### RETRY

**Retrying** (reported by Celery)

This attempt ended with a retry; a new message is on its way.

Celery publishes a NEW message for the same task id with retries+1 and an ETA of now + countdown. Note: RETRY is not a terminal state in Celery (it is in UNREADY_STATES). The ball goes back to the queue.

Settings that change this:

- [`autoretry_for`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/tasks.html#Task.autoretry_for): Retries chosen exceptions automatically.
- [`retry_backoff`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/tasks.html#Task.retry_backoff): Exponential delay between attempts.

### REJECTED

**Rejected** (reported by Celery)

The worker refused the message (requeue=False): dropped, or dead-lettered.

Raised with Reject(requeue=False). If the queue has a dead-letter exchange the broker parks the message in a dead-letter queue; otherwise it is discarded. A rejected task stores no result, so a chord waiting on it is never told. With requeue=True the message goes back to the queue instead (shown as Queued).

Settings that change this:

- [`task_reject_on_worker_lost`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/configuration.html#std-setting-task_reject_on_worker_lost): Requeues (rejects with requeue) when the pool process dies mid-task.

### REVOKED

**Revoked** (reported by Celery)

Cancelled (control.revoke) or expired before it could run.

Sent by revoke, or when a task's expires time passed. If terminated=True the running process was killed with a signal.


### REPLACED

**Replaced** (derived by this monitor)

The task called self.replace(); its id lives on as a different task.

Derived by this monitor. Celery emits no terminal event for the original, so it would look stuck in Running forever. We infer REPLACED when the same task id is published again under a different task name. The new task keeps the old id, which is why a task id is not a unique identity.


### ENDED_SILENTLY

**Ended silently** (derived by this monitor)

No terminal event arrived, but the worker says it is no longer executing this task.

Derived by this monitor by comparing a worker's heartbeat 'active' count with the tasks we believe are running on it. The usual cause is a task that called self.replace() (or raised Ignore): its work continues in other tasks, which is why a chord whose callback can never run leaves its parent here. A lost event looks the same.


### WORKER_LOST

**Worker lost** (derived by this monitor)

The worker running this task stopped sending heartbeats.

Derived by this monitor. A SIGKILL, OOM-kill or lost host emits no event at all, not even worker-offline. What happens next is decided by acks_late: if True and the broker connection dropped, RabbitMQ requeues the message and another worker restarts the task; if False the task is silently lost.

Settings that change this:

- [`task_acks_late`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/tasks.html#Task.acks_late): Without it a dead worker's task is lost.
- [`task_reject_on_worker_lost`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/configuration.html#std-setting-task_reject_on_worker_lost): Covers a pool process dying while its parent worker survives.

### DRAINING

**Draining** (derived by this monitor)

The worker announced shutdown but is still finishing this task.

Celery treats SIGTERM as a WARM shutdown: the worker emits worker-offline, stops taking new work, and lets in-flight tasks complete. If the orchestrator's stop grace period runs out first (docker stop, Kubernetes terminationGracePeriod), the process is killed and the task becomes Worker lost. This is why a deploy is usually safe and a Spot eviction is not.

Settings that change this:

- [`task_acks_late`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/tasks.html#Task.acks_late): If the grace period expires mid-task, this decides whether the task is requeued.

### SUSPECTED_HUNG

**Suspected hung** (derived by this monitor)

Running much longer than expected; Celery cannot tell a hang from a slow job.

Derived by this monitor and only a guess: Celery has no per-task heartbeat. A soft time limit raises an exception inside the task so it can clean up; the hard limit kills the process.

Settings that change this:

- [`task_soft_time_limit`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/tasks.html#Task.soft_time_limit): Raises SoftTimeLimitExceeded inside the task.
- [`task_time_limit`](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/configuration.html#std-setting-task_time_limit): Hard limit: kills the pool process.

### UNKNOWN

**Unknown state** (fallback)

A state this monitor has no description for.

Could be a custom state set with update_state(), or something added by a newer Celery. It is shown generically rather than hidden.
